Alex - thanks for the data and the clear ask. Two practical options from our side:

1) Voucher->Extension: Apply up to 100% of the remaining voucher value to extend the current evaluation by up to 14 days. This preserves your existing SKU/throughput configuration. No additional engineering work, but we require a short amendment to the MSA specifying the extension dates.

2) Voucher->Top-up Capacity: Convert voucher value into a capacity top-up (reserved burst capacity) for the remainder of the trial. This is best if you need more concurrent throughput for nightly batches. There is a small one-time bridging fee for reservation changes (covers provisioning and SLA adjustments).

I've attached a proposed amendment that shows the extension language and the voucher credit calculations. Ben, any ops caveats on the bridging fee estimate?

If Harmonix prefers, we can also do a hybrid: partial voucher applied as credit + 7-day extension.

-Kimberly
